name: The selected permission profile removes the local sandbox
description: The :danger-full-access built-in removes the local sandbox restrictions, so a command the agent composes reaches the whole machine rather than the workspace. A profile selects it through default_permissions or inherits it through extends, and either spelling grants the same reach as the sandbox_mode of the same name.
message: A permission profile removes the local sandbox restrictions

name: A permission profile pulls a path into the workspace
description: A workspace_roots entry makes a path part of the workspace the profile works in, and so sets what a :workspace_roots filesystem key resolves against.
message: A permission profile adds an absolute or home path to the workspace

name: A permission profile grants write access to a path
description: A filesystem entry set to write lets an agent-run command create and overwrite what the path or glob covers. A relative key grants writing inside the workspace the agent was pointed at, which is the posture the :workspace preset itself sets.
message: A permission profile grants write access by an absolute, home or token path rather than a workspace-relative one

name: A permission profile grants read access by an absolute, home or token path
description: A filesystem entry set to read lets an agent-run command open what the path or glob covers. Reading is enough to stage an exfiltration: a credential file the agent can read is a credential it can put in a command it runs. No spelling tells a secret path from a dull one, so this rule takes the same absolute, home or token path its filesystem-write sibling takes, and a reader judges the destination. A relative key reads inside the workspace the agent was pointed at, and a repository-local .env is left out with it: the vendor documents a :workspace_roots glob such as **/*.env as something a profile denies rather than grants.
message: A permission profile grants read access by an absolute, home or token path rather than a workspace-relative one

name: A permission profile opens outbound network traffic
description: The network table's enabled key decides whether a command the agent runs may reach the network at all. Granting it pairs the profile's filesystem reach with egress, which is what turns a file the agent read into a file an attacker receives.
message: A permission profile opens outbound network traffic

name: A host pattern is allowed for outbound traffic
description: A domains entry set to allow names a host the agent may reach. Matching ignores the URL path, so the whole host is reachable however narrow the entry reads, and a host that accepts arbitrary content is an exfiltration route on its own.
message: Outbound traffic to this host pattern is allowed

name: A Unix socket is admitted
description: A unix_sockets entry admits a socket path, and a socket is a channel the network rules never see. A container-runtime control socket or an ssh-agent socket hands the agent host-level control or credential forwarding through a path that reads as a local file.
